newsitem.title: USA: GM unit, NSK form joint venture.
newsitem.headline: GM unit, NSK form joint venture.

text.p: General Motors Corp's Delphi Saginaw Steering Systems said on Tuesday it and Japan's NSK Ltd agreed to jointly market and engineer certain steering and drivetrain components for Asia-Pacific markets.
The two companies said they have formed a joint venture, Delphi Saginaw NSK Co Ltd, which will market the two companies' current lines of continuously variable joints and half-shaft assemblies.
Delphi Saginaw and NSK will engineer new products together, but have agreed to keep their manufacturing operations separate.
A Delphi spokesman, however, said the two firms may consider joint production in the future if customer needs warrant it.

Half shafts and continuously variable joints are key components used in front-wheel drive systems for cars and four-wheel drive trucks. The half shaft transfers power from the transmission to the wheels, while the continuously variable joints allow for steering and suspension movements.
Delphi Saginaw officials said the venture, which will begin operating July 1, will greatly expand the breadth of the two products offered to Japanese automakers worldwide.
Currently, NSK is stronger in half shafts and joints for small cars, while Delphi Saginaw's expertise lies in making the products for larger cars and for trucks.

"Delphi Saginaw Steering and NSK rank number two and four in sales of CVJ (continuously variable joint) and halfshaft products worldwide," Delphi Saginaw general manager Fritz Henderson said in a statement. "Together we are now able to offer our customers the broadest range of CVJ products in the market, combined with the engineering, manufacturing and sales expertise of both companies."
Delphi Saginaw and NSK have a 29-year history of cooperation that includes cross-licensing agreements for various products.
